To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the surface tensile-stress induced by the pad-down force and the surface tensile structure stress in the confined memory cell structure generated a remarkable stress in the confined cross-point memory-cell, resulting in stress corrosion cracking and the generation of the surface polishing voids.

the polishing induced void formation in cross-point phase change memory (PCM) cells is due to surface tensile stress induced stress corrosion cracking, and that the use of a spacer made from SiO2 instead of Si3N4 can prevent the generation of these voids.

surface tensile stress induced polishing voids in cross-point PCMs are generated via stress corrosion cracking mechanism, and the generation frequency and size of the polishing voids are maximized at the maximum surface stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the surface-tensile-stresses induced by the CMP process and its effects on the generation of the voids in the confined memory-cell structures.
the generation of surface-tensile-stresses and the stress corrosion cracking during the CMP of Ge-ST films in the fabrication of phase-change-memory cells.
the generation mechanism of polishing induced voids in cross-point memory cells and a solution to prevent them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the surface tensile-stress induced by CMP is the origin of the polishing induced-voids in the cross-point phase-change memory cell, and the polishing induced- voids are generated via the stress corrosion-cracking.

the generation of polishing induced voids in the fabrication of the cross-point phase-change memory cells was associated with the stress-corrosion cracking, originating from the maximized surface tensiles stress in the confined memory-cell structure.
the generation of polishing induced voids in cross-point memory cells during CMP can be prevented by reducing the surface-tensile-stresses through the design of a spacer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the generation mechanism and the prevention of the polishing induced-voids in the fabrication of crosspoint PCM cells are explained by the surface tensile-stress induced by the confined structure and the surface structure stress.

a design of the cross-point phase-change memory cell using a SiO _{2} spacer is a good solution for the polishing induced void generation problem in the fabrication process of the cross-point memory cells.
the surface tensile stresses induced during CMP can be used as a new process parameter to control the surface roughness and the surface morphology of the Ge-ST films.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polishing induced void generation mechanism in cross-point memory-cells is the stress corrosion cracking, which can be solved by using a SiOx-film spacer rather than a Si3N-film spacer.
the generation frequency and nanometer-scale size of the polishing-induced-voids can be controlled by adjusting the CMP conditions to minimize the maximum surface tensil stress.
a stress corrosion cracking mechanism can be used to understand the generation of polishing induced voids.
